best_overall.name: Kalaya
best_overall.signature_dish: Tom yum with giant river prawns
best_overall.description: Chef Nok Suntaranon's Southern Thai powerhouse earned a James Beard Outstanding Restaurant award for its bold, layered curries and seafood. The lively Fishtown dining room feels celebratory, with ornate dishes and a deep list of Thai flavors rarely seen at this level.

best_overall.name: Zahav
best_overall.description: Michael Solomonov's landmark Israeli restaurant remains a national reference point for modern Middle Eastern cooking. Silky hummus, wood-fire grilling, and gracious service anchor a meal worth planning a trip around.

best_overall.name: Vetri Cucina
best_overall.description: Marc Vetri's long-running temple to Italian fine dining still delivers a flawless, detail-obsessed tasting experience decades in. Impeccable pastas and knowing service keep it among Philadelphia's brightest culinary landmarks.

best_overall.name: Friday Saturday Sunday
best_overall.description: Chad and Hanna Williams' townhouse restaurant earned a Michelin star for its technical, seasonal, and personal contemporary cooking. Warm service and inventive desserts round out one of Philadelphia's most refined nights out.

best_overall.name: Mawn
best_overall.description: This tiny 32-seat BYO from Phila and Rachel Lorn serves modern Cambodian cooking with the energy of a nightly celebration. Cold night-market noodles and chili-laced soups have made it one of the most award-decorated tables in the city.

best_overall.name: Royal Sushi & Izakaya
best_overall.description: Behind a bustling izakaya sits a hidden sushi counter serving one of the city's finest omakase experiences. The front room's flavorful small plates and drinks make it a night that works on two levels.

best_overall.name: Laser Wolf
best_overall.description: This shipudiya from the Zahav team builds a whole meal around live-fire skewers and an endless spread of salads and hummus. The bright room and set format make it a reliably fun group night out.

best_overall.name: Vernick Fish
best_overall.description: Greg Vernick's polished seafood restaurant delivers pristine fish and raw-bar classics in a sleek Comcast-tower setting. Precise cooking and a strong oyster program make it a top-tier special-occasion choice.

best_overall.name: Bastia
best_overall.description: Tyler Akin's coastal Mediterranean spot channels Corsica and the islands with wood-fired seafood and pastas. Bright flavors and an easy, sun-washed vibe make it one of Fishtown's marquee arrivals.

best_overall.name: Her Place Supper Club
best_overall.description: Chef Amanda Shulman's intimate supper club serves a warm, communal set menu that feels like dinner at a very talented friend's home. Its personal, seasonal cooking has made reservations among the hardest to land in the city.

best_overall.name: Pizzeria Beddia
best_overall.signature_dish: The Beddia hoagie and wood-fired pies
best_overall.description: Joe Beddia's pizzeria, once dubbed home of the best pizza in America, serves meticulously crafted pies in a bright, plant-filled room. A patio and natural-wine list round out the low-key but destination-worthy experience.

best_overall.name: Suraya
best_overall.description: A sprawling Lebanese cafe, market, and restaurant with a gorgeous garden patio. Mornings bring pastries and coffee, while dinner delivers mezze and wood-fired kebabs in one of the neighborhood's prettiest spaces.

best_cheesesteaks.name: John's Roast Pork
best_cheesesteaks.signature_dish: Cheesesteak with sharp provolone on a seeded roll
best_cheesesteaks.description: This James Beard-honored corner shop is widely considered the connoisseur's cheesesteak, built on a crusty seeded roll with sharp provolone. Cash-only and daytime-only, it draws lines of purists who prize its balance over hype.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Angelo's Pizzeria
best_cheesesteaks.description: A perpetually packed South Philly pizzeria whose house-baked bread earns it a spot atop many cheesesteak rankings. Expect long waits and a cash-only counter turning out some of the best-constructed steaks in the city.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Pat's King of Steaks
best_cheesesteaks.description: The self-proclaimed birthplace of the cheesesteak, open around the clock at its famous South Philly corner. It's as much a tourist landmark and late-night ritual as a meal, facing off with Geno's across the street.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Geno's Steaks
best_cheesesteaks.description: The neon-drenched rival that has anchored the opposite corner from Pat's for decades. Its brightly lit 24-hour stand is a bucket-list stop for visitors chasing the classic Philly experience.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Tony Luke's
best_cheesesteaks.signature_dish: Cheesesteak and the roast pork Italian
best_cheesesteaks.description: A South Philly legend near the stadiums, famous for both its cheesesteaks and its iconic roast pork Italian with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. The bustling walk-up counter is a game-day and late-night institution.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Dalessandro's Steaks
best_cheesesteaks.description: A Roxborough institution known for finely chopped, juicy meat piled high on a soft roll. Its classic whiz-and-onions steak is a benchmark for locals across the city's northwest.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Woodrow's Sandwich Shop
best_cheesesteaks.description: A modern take on the form, using shaved rib eye and a house-made truffled cheese whiz. The upscale twist has made it a favorite for those wanting something beyond the traditional sandwich.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Joe's Steaks + Soda Shop
best_cheesesteaks.description: A retro shop turning out griddled steaks from a recipe that's barely changed in 60 years. The old-school soda-fountain milkshakes make it a fun, family-friendly Fishtown stop.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Jim's South St.
best_cheesesteaks.description: A South Street icon that reopened after a major fire and is once again griddling its beloved steaks in a rebuilt space. The aroma pouring onto the sidewalk still pulls in a steady line of locals and tourists.

best_cheesesteaks.name: Cleavers
best_cheesesteaks.description: A sleek Center City counter that has become a modern go-to, favoring quality beef and gooey Cooper Sharp cheese. Its polished, quick-service format suits the downtown lunch crowd.

best_fishtown.name: Kalaya
best_fishtown.signature_dish: Tom yum with giant river prawns
best_fishtown.description: Nok Suntaranon's award-winning Southern Thai flagship is Fishtown's crown jewel, serving vivid curries and whole grilled fish. The stylish, buzzy room makes it a destination worth booking well ahead.

best_fishtown.name: Laser Wolf
best_fishtown.description: The Zahav team's live-fire shipudiya builds a full meal around grilled skewers and an endless spread of salads, pita, and hummus. The set-price format and lively vibe make it a great group destination.

best_fishtown.name: Suraya
best_fishtown.description: A sprawling Lebanese cafe, market, and restaurant with a gorgeous garden patio. Mornings bring pastries and coffee, while dinner delivers mezze and wood-fired kebabs in one of the neighborhood's prettiest spaces.

best_fishtown.name: Wm. Mulherin's Sons
best_fishtown.description: Set in a restored former whiskey distillery, this rustic-chic restaurant turns out wood-fired pizzas and Italian plates. The handsome, brick-and-timber room also anchors a boutique hotel upstairs.

best_fishtown.name: Middle Child Clubhouse
best_fishtown.description: The sit-down big sibling of the beloved Middle Child luncheonette, serving inventive sandwiches by day and a whimsical American menu by night. Its playful, retro-clubhouse energy makes it a Fishtown favorite.

best_fishtown.name: Amá
best_fishtown.description: An upscale modern Mexican restaurant with sharp regional cooking and a serious cocktail program. Dishes like crisp tostadas and inventive small plates give it a polished, date-night energy.

best_fishtown.name: Bastia
best_fishtown.description: Tyler Akin's coastal Mediterranean spot channels Corsica with wood-fired seafood and bright, sun-washed pastas. It's one of the most talked-about recent additions to the neighborhood.

best_fishtown.name: El Chingon
best_fishtown.description: A casual, craveable taqueria known for its in-house baked tortas and sourdough flour tortillas. Bold salsas and a relaxed vibe make it a reliable neighborhood go-to.

best_fishtown.name: Pizzeria Beddia
best_fishtown.description: Joe Beddia's pizzeria, once dubbed home of the best pizza in America, serves meticulously crafted pies in a bright, plant-filled room. A patio and natural-wine list round out the low-key but destination-worthy experience.

best_fishtown.name: Frankford Hall
best_fishtown.description: Stephen Starr's sprawling beer garden pours giant steins alongside pretzels, sausages, and pub fare. Communal tables, ping-pong, and fire pits make it a go-to for a big, laid-back group hang.
